note: Private mutation/regression corpus for SwiftInferProperties — the inference engine dogfooding on itself (Chapter 30 §30.4.4). Three families: mutants in the IdempotenceWitnessDetector's own name-classifier; mutants that undo a name-only-position guard (a key-path component's or a member's name read as a test-local); and mutants that undo one piece of the construction-facts wiring (the scan dropping its table, re-parsing the trees the table was built from, the universe admitting test targets, a test-directory scan walking up, the census replica going blind to the construction witness). Each is killed by its own code's unit tests, which pin both what it should and should not do. Run via `swift test --filter`. Not a scored benchmark.

mutants.label: drop `reset` from the exact-name set — a genuinely idempotent action is no longer recognized as a witness
add `increment` to the exact-name set — a non-idempotent action is falsely classified as an idempotence witness
drop the `set` prefix — `setX`-style assignments are no longer recognized as prefix-match witnesses
ReceiverConstructionHarvester's free-name check skips member names only — `\.name` reads as a test-local and `Sorter(by: \.name)` is never harvested
ReceiverConstructionHarvester's inliner rewrites key-path names — `let pageSize = 10` harvests `Pager(sortedBy: \.10, pageSize: 10)`
the Slicer's identifier collector records member and key-path names — `.map(\.id)` and `{ $0.id }` pull an unrelated `let id = 7` into the property region
LocalBindingResolver substitutes into a key-path name — `let id = makeID()` makes `\.makeID()`, a component whose declName slot holds a call
MinedTraceSelector counts every lowercase name as a test-local — `Feature.State(color: .red)` and `Feature.State(sort: \.name)` are dropped
MinedTraceSelector skips every member name, not only key-path and leading-dot ones — `Feature.State(items: Self.fixtureItems)` is kept, pasted into the verifier stub, and fails its build
MinedTraceSelector reads `Self` as a type — `Self.Fixture()` names the test suite and is kept for a stub where `Self` is the stub
LocalBindingResolver skips everything inside a key path — `\.[id]` keeps the unresolved local where its argument should be substituted
ReceiverConstructionHarvester's inliner skips everything inside a key path — `Sorter(by: \.[index])` keeps the test-local

the package scan builds its ConstructionFacts and hands the visitor the unconfigured oracle — the table is built and dropped on the way, and a sibling target's `let id = UUID()` no longer refutes its constructor
the scan re-parses every judged file instead of reusing the universe's tree — SEI types an assignment by node identity, so `reset` is refuted by another target's same-named `A`
the universe predicate stops rejecting `Tests` / `*Tests` directories — a test target's `struct Item { let id = UUID() }` refutes a production `make() -> Item`
a scan under `Tests/Fixtures/X` walks up to the enclosing package — whose rule drops the fixture's own files, so its types never reach its table
the census replica stops consulting SEI's construction witness — 0 verdicts move on Sources/, so verdictAgreesWithSoundPurity stays green while 2 re-witnessed rows are filed as ignorance
